page: Microsoft Azure FX12-6ms_v2 is a specialized instance designed for workloads requiring high single-core clock speeds paired with an exceptionally large memory footprint. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz, this x86_64 instance provides 6 dedicated vCPUs across 3 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem features 260 MB of L3 cache alongside support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix acceleration. The instance is configured with 252.0 GB of system memory, providing 42.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. No local storage is bundled, and it does not include discrete GPUs.

Performance benchmarks reflect the high-frequency architecture and restrained core count. The instance achieves top-tier results in single-threaded operations, including a Geekbench single-core score of 2350.0 and strong throughput in single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. Text processing operations also place in the top decile. Conversely, aggregate multi-threaded metrics such as PassMark CPU (12016.38) and multi-core Geekbench (7274.0) track in the median tier due to the 6-vCPU boundary. Memory bandwidth reaches 50.68 GB/sec for uncached read blocks, supporting heavy data exchange to cache.

Given its unique ratio of high compute frequency to massive memory density without local disk, FX12-6ms_v2 offers high qualitative efficiency for licensing models tied to core counts. It is well suited for memory-bound electronic design automation (EDA), financial modeling, in-memory databases, relational database engines with high cache requirements, and batch analytics jobs where high single-thread execution velocity is critical.
